newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel ethylene maker shuts plant for repairs.
newsitem.headline: Israel ethylene maker shuts plant for repairs.

text.p: Israel's Carmel Olefins Ltd has shut down its ethylene plant in Haifa for four weeks for repairs, an official at state-controlled Oil Refineries, one of the joint owners of the company, said on Thursday.
Carmel is Israel's only producer of ethylene, which is used as a raw material in the petrochemical industry.
One of the companies that will be affected by the shutdown is Electrochemical Industries (Frutarom) Ltd, which produces PVC and receives its ethylene supply from the Haifa plant.

A senior Frutarom official said its PVC production would be cut in half during the coming month due to the drop in ethylene supplies. But he did not expect this to have an adverse affect on the company as it would continue to supply customers from its inventory.

Carmel is Israel's largest petrochemical company and the predominant supplier of raw materials to the country's plastics industry. It is owned jointly by Oil Refineries and Israel Petrochemical Enterprises Ltd.
Oil Refineries is 74 percent owned by the government and 26 percent by Israel Corp, one of the country's biggest holding concerns.
